agent_outputs.summary: UserService and OrderService share a single module with a clear domain seam. At scale this coupling will slow independent deploys; a service split is worth considering.
agent_outputs.top_priority: Decompose UserService along the domain boundary visible at src/services/users.py:234.

findings.description: UserService and OrderService are entangled in one module. There is a clean domain boundary at src/services/users.py:234. Recommend decomposing into two microservices so each team can deploy independently and scale hot paths separately.
findings.recommendation: Extract OrderService into its own deployable service communicating over an internal API, with UserService as a separate bounded context.

agent_outputs.summary: Current auth is a single in-process check. The proposed microservice split would introduce inter-service auth and materially expand the attack surface.
agent_outputs.top_priority: Do not split into services at this scale without an inter-service auth design — it adds four new attack classes.

findings.description: Auth is a single in-process middleware check at src/middleware/auth.py:18. Adequate for a monolith. Splitting into services would replace this with JWT passed between services, introducing token forgery, replay, key-distribution, and man-in-the-middle risks that do not exist today.
findings.recommendation: Keep the in-process check. If a split is ever required, design mTLS or a signed service-to-service token scheme first.

agent_outputs.summary: The coupling the Architect flagged is real but shallow — a single shared helper, not deep entanglement.
agent_outputs.top_priority: Extract the shared helper into a module boundary before considering any service split.

findings.description: The coupling between UserService and OrderService is a single shared function _resolve_account() at src/services/users.py:240. This is a module-level smell, not architecture-level entanglement — it can be broken with an extraction, no new services required.
findings.recommendation: Move _resolve_account() into a shared accounts module and have both services import it. Reassess boundaries after that.

discussion_turns.message: CHALLENGE architect_1: decomposition introduces JWT inter-service auth — four new attack vectors (token forgery, replay, key distribution, MITM) that do not exist in the current in-process model at src/middleware/auth.py:18. At under 1,000 users the scaling benefit does not justify tripling the auth attack surface.

CHALLENGE architect_1: the coupling is one shared function, _resolve_account() at src/services/users.py:240 — not deep entanglement. A module extraction achieves the separation you want without standing up new services or the operational overhead that implies.

CONCEDING security_1: the security cost is valid at current scale, and code_reviewer_1 is right that the coupling is shallow. Withdrawing the microservices recommendation. A modular monolith with an extracted accounts module gives the domain boundary without the new attack surface. Revisit services past ~50k users.

consensus_report.executive_summary: The Architect proposed splitting this application into microservices for cleaner boundaries. The Security Engineer pushed back: at this scale the split would add four new authentication attack vectors for little real benefit, and the Code Reviewer showed the coupling is a single shared function, not deep entanglement. The team converged on a modular monolith — extract the shared code into its own module now, and reconsider services only when traffic justifies it. This is exactly the cross-domain trade-off a single AI reviewer cannot make, because it requires one specialist to overrule another.

findings.description: Adopt a modular monolith: extract the shared _resolve_account() helper into an accounts module to create the domain boundary, without splitting into separately deployed services. Supersedes the original microservices proposal (architect_1) after Security and Code Reviewer challenges.
findings.recommendation: Extract src/services/users.py:240 into a shared accounts module imported by both UserService and OrderService. Do not introduce inter-service auth at current scale.

findings.description: Keep the in-process auth check; a service split would expand the attack surface with JWT inter-service auth.
findings.recommendation: Retain in-process auth; design mTLS/signed tokens before any future split.

conflicts_resolved.reason: The Architect recommended microservices (confidence 78%). The Security Engineer challenged at 91% confidence that a split introduces four new JWT-based attack vectors absent from the current in-process model, disproportionate to the benefit at under 1,000 users. The Code Reviewer independently showed the coupling was a single shared function, not deep entanglement. The Architect conceded in round 2 and withdrew the recommendation. Resolution: modular monolith — the domain boundary is achieved by a module extraction, and services are revisited only past ~50k users.
